standard: WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition (CNS5, 2021)

gradingConvention.note: WHO CNS5 replaced Roman numerals with Arabic numerals across all CNS tumor types, adopted within-tumor-type grading (e.g., Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 2, 3, or 4), and integrated molecular hallmarks that can establish CNS WHO grade 3 or 4 independent of histology.

NOS.label: Not Otherwise Specified (NOS)
NOS.definition: Indicates that diagnostic information (typically molecular testing) required to assign a specific WHO CNS5 entity is unavailable, not performed, or failed technically.
NOS.action: Recommend reflex molecular testing (IDH1/2 sequencing, 1p/19q FISH/NGS, CDKN2A/B, TERT/EGFR/+7/-10, H3/MAPK/fusion panel, or genome-wide DNA methylation profiling).

NEC.label: Not Elsewhere Classified (NEC)
NEC.definition: Indicates that required diagnostic testing was successfully performed, but the integrated histological-molecular results are discordant or do not conform to any recognized WHO CNS5 diagnosis.
NEC.action: Perform orthogonal confirmation (e.g., whole-arm vs. partial 1p/19q copy-number analysis, RNA fusion sequencing, genome-wide DNA methylation classifier) and discuss at multidisciplinary neuro-oncology tumor board.

families.label: Adult-Type Diffuse Gliomas
families.description: IDH-mutant astrocytoma (CNS WHO grade 2, 3, or 4), IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma (CNS WHO grade 2 or 3), and IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (CNS WHO grade 4, including molecular GBM).

entities.name: Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant
molecularHallmarks: IDH1 or IDH2 missense mutation (canonical IDH1 p.R132H or non-canonical IDH1/2)
1p/19q intact (or unequivocal ATRX loss obviating mandatory 1p/19q testing)
ATRX loss / mutation and TP53 mutation (typical astrocytic immunophenotype)
CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion (sufficient for CNS WHO grade 4 independent of necrosis or MVP)
histologicHallmarks: Diffusely infiltrating astrocytic glioma
CNS WHO grade 2: well-differentiated, low mitotic activity, no necrosis or MVP
CNS WHO grade 3: focal or dispersed anaplasia and significant mitotic activity
CNS WHO grade 4: microvascular proliferation and/or necrosis (or CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion)
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 retired the term 'Glioblastoma, IDH-mutant' in favor of 'Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4'.
Homozygous CDKN2A/B deletion automatically upgrades Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant to CNS WHO grade 4 even in histologically grade 2 or 3 tumors.
For residual or recurrent CNS WHO grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma, evaluate vorasidenib (dual IDH1/2 inhibitor; INDIGO trial).

entities.name: Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted
molecularHallmarks: IDH1 or IDH2 mutation
Combined whole-arm 1p/19q codeletion
TERT promoter mutation (very frequent) and ATRX retained
CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion (adverse prognostic marker; may support CNS WHO grade 3 in histologically borderline/equivocal cases, but not an unconditional standalone molecular upgrade)
histologicHallmarks: Diffusely infiltrating glioma with uniform rounded nuclei, perinuclear halos, and branching chicken-wire capillaries
CNS WHO grade 2: low mitotic activity, no MVP or necrosis
CNS WHO grade 3: brisk mitotic activity (>=6 mitoses/10 HPF or >=2.5/mm2), microvascular proliferation, and/or necrosis
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 retired the qualifier 'anaplastic'; grade 3 tumors are termed 'Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, CNS WHO grade 3'.
Evaluate vorasidenib (INDIGO phase 3 trial) for residual or recurrent CNS WHO grade 2 disease.
Typically exhibits high sensitivity to alkylating chemotherapy (PCV or temozolomide) and near-universal MGMT promoter methylation.

entities.name: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype
molecularHallmarks: IDH-wildtype and H3-wildtype
TERT promoter mutation (sufficient for molecular GBM grade 4)
EGFR gene amplification (sufficient for molecular GBM grade 4)
Combined gain of chromosome 7 and loss of chromosome 10 (+7/-10) (sufficient for molecular GBM grade 4)
histologicHallmarks: Diffusely infiltrating astrocytic glioma
Microvascular proliferation (MVP)
Necrosis (pseudopalisading or geographic)
companionNotes: Molecular GBM rule (cIMPACT-NOW Update 3 / WHO CNS5): An adult IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytic glioma lacking necrosis and MVP is classified as Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype (CNS WHO grade 4) if >=1 of TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification, or +7/-10 copy-number change is present.
MGMT promoter methylation predicts improved overall survival and greater benefit from temozolomide alkylating chemotherapy (Stupp/Hegi).
In patients <55 years with negative IDH1 p.R132H IHC, IDH1/2 sequencing and H3 K27/G34 exclusion are recommended before finalizing IDH-wildtype status.

families.label: Pediatric-Type Diffuse High-Grade Gliomas
families.description: Diffuse midline glioma H3 K27-altered, diffuse hemispheric glioma H3 G34-mutant, diffuse pediatric-type HGG H3-wt/IDH-wt, and infant-type hemispheric glioma.

entities.name: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered
molecularHallmarks: Global loss of nuclear H3 K27me3 (unifying epigenetic hallmark)
H3.3 (H3-3A) or H3.1/H3.2 (H3C2/H3C3) p.K28M (K27M) mutation
EZHIP overexpression (H3-wildtype DMG subtype)
EGFR mutation or amplification in midline/bithalamic DMG subtype
histologicHallmarks: Diffusely infiltrating glioma centered in midline structures (pons/brainstem, thalamus, spinal cord)
Assigned CNS WHO grade 4 regardless of low-grade or bland biopsy histology
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 broadened 'H3 K27M-mutant' to 'H3 K27-altered' to encompass EZHIP-overexpressing and EGFR-mutant midline subtypes.
Strictly requires midline anatomic localization; non-midline H3 K27M-mutant gliomas should be reported with NEC/methylation review rather than automatically called DMG.
Evaluate clinical trial eligibility including dordaviprone (ONC201) and cellular/immunotherapy protocols.

entities.name: Diffuse hemispheric glioma, H3 G34-mutant
molecularHallmarks: H3-3A p.G35R or p.G35V (G34R/G34V) missense mutation
ATRX loss/mutation and TP53 mutation (nearly universal)
OLIG2-negative immunophenotype and frequent MGMT promoter methylation
histologicHallmarks: Diffusely infiltrating high-grade glioma of the cerebral hemispheres
Glioblastoma-like or embryonal/PNET-like high-grade morphology
companionNotes: Predominantly affects adolescents and young adults; always assigned CNS WHO grade 4.
High rate of MGMT promoter methylation supports evaluation of temozolomide-based regimens.

entities.name: Diffuse pediatric-type high-grade glioma, H3-wildtype and IDH-wildtype
molecularHallmarks: IDH-wildtype and H3-wildtype
DNA methylation classes: pHGG RTK1 (PDGFRA amp / radiation- or Lynch-associated), pHGG RTK2 (EGFR amp / TERT), or pHGG MYCN (MYCN amp)
histologicHallmarks: Diffusely infiltrating high-grade glioma in children or young adults
Brisk mitotic activity with or without microvascular proliferation and necrosis
companionNotes: Evaluate for constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (CMMRD) or Lynch syndrome (particularly in hypermutant pHGG RTK1), which may predict response to PD-1 checkpoint blockade.
pHGG MYCN carries the poorest prognosis among the three methylation subclasses.

entities.name: Infant-type hemispheric glioma
molecularHallmarks: Recurrent receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) gene fusions involving NTRK1/2/3, ROS1, ALK, or MET
Distinct infant hemispheric glioma DNA methylation signature
histologicHallmarks: Cellular, often high-grade-appearing astrocytic glioma arising in the cerebral hemispheres during infancy/early childhood
Frequent sharp circumscription or palisading necrosis despite favorable targeted-therapy outcomes
companionNotes: Actionable RTK fusions enable targeted kinase inhibitor therapy (e.g., larotrectinib/entrectinib for NTRK/ROS1; alectinib/lorlatinib for ALK), potentially avoiding cranial irradiation in infants.
No formal CNS WHO grade is assigned in WHO CNS5 given distinct natural history and targeted therapy responsiveness.

families.label: Pediatric-Type Diffuse Low-Grade Gliomas
families.description: IDH-wildtype and H3-wildtype pediatric-type diffuse low-grade gliomas driven by MYB/MYBL1 or MAPK pathway alterations (including angiocentric glioma and PLNTY).

entities.name: Diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered
molecularHallmarks: Structural alteration (fusion or amplification/rearrangement) of MYB or MYBL1
IDH-wildtype and H3-wildtype
histologicHallmarks: Monomorphic, diffusely infiltrating astrocytic cells in cerebral cortex/white matter
Low cellularity, absent or rare mitoses, no necrosis or MVP; often epileptogenic
companionNotes: Assigned CNS WHO grade 1 with generally indolent clinical course and high rates of seizure freedom after surgical resection.

entities.name: Angiocentric glioma
molecularHallmarks: MYB::QKI gene fusion (canonical alteration in the vast majority of cases)
IDH-wildtype and H3-wildtype
histologicHallmarks: Bipolar spindle-shaped glial cells forming perivascular angiocentric rosettes
Subpial palisading and dot-like EMA positivity
companionNotes: Assigned CNS WHO grade 1; strongly associated with medically refractory epilepsy in children and young adults.

entities.name: Polymorphous low-grade neuroepithelial tumor of the young (PLNTY)
molecularHallmarks: MAPK pathway alteration: BRAF p.V600E mutation or FGFR2/FGFR3 gene fusion (e.g., FGFR2::CTNNA3, FGFR3::TACC3)
IDH-wildtype and 1p/19q intact
histologicHallmarks: Infiltrative oligodendroglioma-like components with frequent prominent calcifications
Strong diffuse regional CD34 immunoreactivity in tumor cells and ramified cortical neural elements
companionNotes: Assigned CNS WHO grade 1; overwhelmingly epileptogenic and typically located in the temporal lobe of children and young adults.

entities.name: Diffuse low-grade glioma, MAPK pathway-altered
molecularHallmarks: MAPK pathway driver: BRAF p.V600E, FGFR1 TKD duplication/mutation/fusion, BRAF fusion, NF1, or other MAPK alteration
IDH-wildtype, H3-wildtype, and CDKN2A/B intact
histologicHallmarks: Diffuse low-grade astrocytic or oligodendroglioma-like morphology without high-grade anaplasia
Absence of classic PLNTY or angiocentric glioma diagnostic features
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 recommends reporting the specific molecular alteration (e.g., FGFR1-mutant or BRAF V600E-mutant) to guide targeted MAPK therapy.
For BRAF V600E-mutant pediatric LGG, dabrafenib + trametinib is FDA-approved; for BRAF fusions, evaluate type 2 pan-RAF inhibition (tovorafenib) or MEK inhibition and avoid type 1 BRAF monotherapy.

families.label: Circumscribed Astrocytic Gliomas
families.description: Pilocytic astrocytoma, high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features (HGAP), pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma (PXA), SEGA, chordoid glioma, and MN1-altered astroblastoma.

entities.name: Pilocytic astrocytoma
molecularHallmarks: KIAA1549::BRAF gene fusion (most common, especially posterior fossa)
Alternative MAPK drivers: NF1 inactivation (optic pathway), BRAF p.V600E, FGFR1, PTPN11, RAF1 fusions
histologicHallmarks: Biphasic compact piloid and loose microcystic architecture
Rosenthal fibers and eosinophilic granular bodies
companionNotes: Assigned CNS WHO grade 1; microvascular proliferation and occasional necrosis do not confer high-grade status in classic pilocytic astrocytoma.
If CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and anaplastic features are present (especially in adults), evaluate DNA methylation for HGAP.

entities.name: High-grade astrocytoma with piloid features
molecularHallmarks: Characteristic HGAP genome-wide DNA methylation profile (essential criterion)
Frequent triad of MAPK pathway alteration (NF1/BRAF/FGFR1), CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, and ATRX loss/mutation
histologicHallmarks: Astrocytic glioma with variable piloid features, Rosenthal fibers, and high-grade mitotic activity/necrosis/MVP
Frequently arises in the cerebellum of adults
companionNotes: First newly recognized WHO CNS5 entity whose definitive diagnosis requires DNA methylation profiling.
Clinical outcome roughly parallels CNS WHO grade 3 IDH-mutant astrocytoma, though formal CNS WHO grade is not yet assigned.

entities.name: Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma
molecularHallmarks: BRAF p.V600E mutation (~60-80% of cases) or other MAPK alteration
CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion (~90% of cases)
histologicHallmarks: Circumscribed superficial/meningocortical glioma with pleomorphic, lipidized xanthomatous cells, eosinophilic granular bodies, and pericellular reticulin network
CNS WHO grade 3 defined by >=5 mitoses per 10 HPF (>=2.5 mitoses/mm2)
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 retired the modifier 'anaplastic'; tumors meeting the mitotic threshold are classified as Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 3.
Evaluate BRAF/MEK targeted therapy in recurrent or unresectable BRAF V600E-mutant PXA.

entities.name: Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma
molecularHallmarks: Biallelic inactivation of TSC1 or TSC2 leading to constitutive mTORC1 activation
histologicHallmarks: Well-circumscribed intraventricular tumor near the foramen of Monro
Large ganglion-like/gemistocytic astrocytes with abundant glassy eosinophilic cytoplasm and calcifications
companionNotes: Assigned CNS WHO grade 1; clinical hallmark of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC).
mTOR inhibitor everolimus is FDA-approved for TSC-associated SEGA requiring therapeutic intervention when curative resection is not feasible.

entities.name: Chordoid glioma
molecularHallmarks: Recurrent PRKCA p.D463H missense mutation (hallmark driver)
histologicHallmarks: Well-circumscribed anterior third ventricular tumor
Cords and clusters of GFAP-positive, TTF1-positive epithelioid tumor cells within mucinous stroma with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
companionNotes: Assigned CNS WHO grade 2; despite slow growth, surgical morbidity is high due to hypothalamic proximity.

entities.name: Astroblastoma, MN1-altered
molecularHallmarks: Structural rearrangement of MN1 (most commonly MN1::BEND2 or MN1::CXXC5 fusion)
Distinct CNS HGNET-MN1 DNA methylation class
histologicHallmarks: Circumscribed hemispheric tumor predominantly in children/young women
Prominent astroblastic perivascular pseudorosettes with broad, stout processes and vascular hyalinization
companionNotes: No formal CNS WHO grade is assigned in WHO CNS5; local recurrences are common, though overall survival is often prolonged.

families.label: Ependymal Tumors
families.description: Anatomically and molecularly defined ependymomas across supratentorial, posterior fossa, and spinal compartments, plus myxopapillary ependymoma (CNS WHO grade 2) and subependymoma (grade 1).

entities.name: Supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion-positive
molecularHallmarks: ZFTA (formerly C11orf95) gene fusion, most commonly ZFTA::RELA or alternative partners (MAML2, NCOA1/2)
CDKN2A homozygous deletion (adverse prognostic modifier)
histologicHallmarks: Supratentorial ependymoma with perivascular pseudorosettes, clear-cell or branching capillary areas
CNS WHO grade 2 vs. grade 3 determined by mitotic activity, microvascular proliferation, and cellularity/anaplasia
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 replaced 'RELA fusion-positive' with 'ZFTA fusion-positive' to capture non-RELA ZFTA fusion partners.
Generally carries worse progression-free survival than YAP1 fusion-positive supratentorial ependymoma.

entities.name: Supratentorial ependymoma, YAP1 fusion-positive
molecularHallmarks: YAP1 gene fusion, most commonly YAP1::MAMLD1 or YAP1::FAM118B
histologicHallmarks: Supratentorial ependymoma arising predominantly in infants and young children
Perivascular pseudorosettes; CNS WHO grade 2 or 3 by histological anaplasia
companionNotes: Associated with a distinctly favorable prognosis compared to ZFTA fusion-positive supratentorial ependymoma.

entities.name: Posterior fossa group A (PFA) ependymoma
molecularHallmarks: Global loss of nuclear H3 K27me3 (typically driven by EZHIP overexpression)
PFA DNA methylation profile
Chromosome 1q gain and 6q loss (high-risk prognostic markers)
histologicHallmarks: Posterior fossa ependymoma with perivascular pseudorosettes and/or true ependymal rosettes
CNS WHO grade 2 or 3 based on mitotic activity and anaplastic features
companionNotes: Predominantly occurs in infants and young children; carries significantly higher recurrence risk and worse survival than PFB ependymoma.

entities.name: Posterior fossa group B (PFB) ependymoma
molecularHallmarks: Retained nuclear H3 K27me3 immunostaining
PFB DNA methylation profile with frequent broad chromosomal instability
histologicHallmarks: Posterior fossa ependymoma predominantly in older children and adults
CNS WHO grade 2 or 3 based on histological features
companionNotes: Significantly more favorable prognosis than PFA ependymoma; maximal safe resection is a primary determinant of long-term control.

entities.name: Spinal ependymoma
molecularHallmarks: Chromosome 22q loss and NF2 mutation (frequent)
Absence of MYCN amplification
histologicHallmarks: Circumscribed intramedullary spinal cord ependymoma with perivascular pseudorosettes
CNS WHO grade 2 or 3 based on mitotic activity and anaplasia
companionNotes: Evaluate for NF2-related schwannomatosis in young patients or those with multifocal spinal tumors.

entities.name: Spinal ependymoma, MYCN-amplified
molecularHallmarks: High-level MYCN gene amplification (essential diagnostic criterion)
Distinct DNA methylation class separate from conventional spinal ependymoma
histologicHallmarks: Predominantly extramedullary/intradural cervicothoracic spinal ependymoma with high-grade histological features
Brisk mitoses, microvascular proliferation, necrosis, and strong MYCN nuclear protein expression
companionNotes: Newly defined aggressive WHO CNS5 molecular entity with high rates of early recurrence and leptomeningeal dissemination despite surgical resection.

entities.name: Myxopapillary ependymoma
molecularHallmarks: Distinct myxopapillary ependymoma DNA methylation profile (often with chromosomal instability/gains)
histologicHallmarks: Tumor of the conus medullaris, cauda equina, or filum terminale
Radial arrangement of cuboidal-to-elongated GFAP-positive cells around vascularized myxoid/hyalinized stromal cores
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 upgraded Myxopapillary ependymoma from grade 1 (2016 4th edition update) to CNS WHO grade 2 due to recurrence rates comparable to conventional spinal ependymoma.

entities.name: Subependymoma
molecularHallmarks: Compartment-specific subependymoma DNA methylation classes (supratentorial, posterior fossa, spinal); TERT promoter mutations may occur in a subset without altering grade
histologicHallmarks: Clusters of uniform bland glial nuclei embedded in a dense fibrillary matrix with microcysts
Absent or negligible mitotic activity
companionNotes: Assigned CNS WHO grade 1 with excellent prognosis; frequently incidental or cured by resection.

families.label: Meningiomas
families.description: Single WHO CNS5 tumor type with 15 histological subtypes graded CNS WHO grade 1, 2, or 3 using combined histological criteria and molecular grade 3 drivers (TERT promoter mutation or CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion).

entities.name: Meningioma
molecularHallmarks: TERT promoter mutation (automatic CNS WHO grade 3 independent of histology)
CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion (automatic CNS WHO grade 3 independent of histology)
H3 K27me3 loss (adverse recurrence biomarker, especially in grade 1/2 meningiomas)
BAP1 loss (rhabdoid/high-grade meningioma; BAP1 predisposition syndrome)
SMARCE1 loss (clear cell meningioma; hereditary predisposition)
Subtype drivers: NF2 (convexity/fibrous/transitional), TRAF7/KLF4 (secretory), AKT1/SMO/PIK3CA (skull base)
histologicHallmarks: CNS WHO grade 1: <4 mitoses/10 HPF, no brain invasion, <3 atypical features, and non-chordoid/non-clear-cell subtype

CNS WHO grade 2: 4-19 mitoses/10 HPF, OR brain invasion, OR >=3 of 5 atypical features (hypercellularity, small cell change, prominent nucleoli, sheet-like growth, spontaneous necrosis), OR chordoid/clear cell subtype
CNS WHO grade 3: >=20 mitoses/10 HPF, OR frank anaplasia (sarcoma-/carcinoma-/melanoma-like), OR TERT promoter mutation / CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion
companionNotes: WHO CNS5 considers meningioma a single tumor type with 15 subtypes and applies grading criteria across all subtypes.
Major CNS5 update: Rhabdoid and papillary subtypes are NO LONGER automatically CNS WHO grade 3; they are graded using standard histological and molecular criteria.
TERT promoter mutation or CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion immediately establishes CNS WHO grade 3 regardless of benign-appearing histology.

families.label: Medulloblastomas
families.description: Molecularly defined CNS WHO grade 4 embryonal tumors: WNT-activated, SHH-activated TP53-wildtype, SHH-activated TP53-mutant, and non-WNT/non-SHH (Group 3 / Group 4).

entities.name: Medulloblastoma, WNT-activated
molecularHallmarks: CTNNB1 exon 3 activating mutation (or germline APC mutation in CTNNB1-wildtype cases)
Nuclear beta-catenin accumulation and monosomy 6
WNT DNA methylation class
histologicHallmarks: Predominantly classic medulloblastoma morphology arising in dorsal brainstem/cerebellopontine angle
Assigned CNS WHO grade 4
companionNotes: Most favorable medulloblastoma group (>90-95% 5-year survival in pediatric cohorts); focus of radiotherapy de-escalation trials.
Test for germline APC mutation (Turcot/FAP syndrome) if CTNNB1 sequencing is wildtype.

entities.name: Medulloblastoma, SHH-activated and TP53-wildtype
molecularHallmarks: SHH pathway activation (PTCH1, SMO, SUFU mutations; GLI2 amplification; TERT promoter mutation in adults)
TP53-wildtype
SHH DNA methylation subgroups (SHH-1 to SHH-4)
histologicHallmarks: Classic, desmoplastic/nodular, or medulloblastoma with extensive nodularity (MBEN); rarely large cell/anaplastic
Assigned CNS WHO grade 4
companionNotes: Evaluate for germline PTCH1 or SUFU mutations (Gorlin syndrome), particularly in infants and young children with desmoplastic/nodular or MBEN histology.
Intermediate overall prognosis; infants with desmoplastic/nodular or MBEN histology have favorable outcomes with radiation-sparing chemotherapy.

entities.name: Medulloblastoma, SHH-activated and TP53-mutant
molecularHallmarks: SHH pathway activation combined with somatic or germline TP53 mutation
Frequent chromothripsis and MYCN or GLI2 amplification
histologicHallmarks: Frequently large cell/anaplastic histology, typically in older children/adolescents
Assigned CNS WHO grade 4
companionNotes: Urgent cancer genetics referral for germline TP53 testing (Li-Fraumeni syndrome) is mandatory.
Very high-risk prognosis with heightened susceptibility to radiation-induced secondary malignancies in Li-Fraumeni carriers.

entities.name: Medulloblastoma, non-WNT/non-SHH
molecularHallmarks: Group 3 (MYC amplification, GFI1/GFI1B activation, isochromosome 17q) or Group 4 (PRDM6 activation, KDM6A, MYCN/CDK6 amplification, isochromosome 17q)
WHO CNS5 subdivides non-WNT/non-SHH into 8 molecular subgroups (subgroups 1-8) by DNA methylation profiling
histologicHallmarks: Classic or large cell/anaplastic histology
Assigned CNS WHO grade 4
companionNotes: MYC amplification (predominantly Group 3) and metastatic disease (M+) denote very high risk.
Group 4 is the most common medulloblastoma group overall and typically has intermediate prognosis.

mgmt_methylated.name: MGMT Promoter Methylation
mgmt_methylated.summary: Associated with improved overall survival and greater benefit from temozolomide alkylating chemotherapy in Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype (Stupp et al., NEJM 2005; Hegi et al., NEJM 2005).

vorasidenib_idh_grade2.name: Vorasidenib (Dual IDH1/2 Inhibitor)
vorasidenib_idh_grade2.summary: INDIGO phase 3 trial (Mellinghoff et al., NEJM 2023) demonstrated significantly prolonged progression-free survival and time to next intervention in residual or recurrent CNS WHO grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma.

braf_mek_pediatric_lgg.name: BRAF / MEK / Pan-RAF Targeted Therapy
braf_mek_pediatric_lgg.summary: Dabrafenib + trametinib is FDA-approved for BRAF V600E-mutant pediatric LGG (Bouffet et al., NEJM 2023); tovorafenib (type 2 pan-RAF inhibitor) is active across BRAF fusions (KIAA1549::BRAF) and BRAF V600E (FIREFLY-1).

rtk_fusion_infant.name: Actionable RTK Fusions (NTRK/ROS1/ALK/MET)
rtk_fusion_infant.summary: Infant-type hemispheric gliomas frequently harbor targetable receptor tyrosine kinase fusions (e.g., larotrectinib/entrectinib for NTRK/ROS1; alectinib/lorlatinib for ALK), enabling radiation-sparing systemic therapy.

everolimus_sega.name: mTOR Inhibition (Everolimus)
everolimus_sega.summary: FDA-approved systemic therapy for TSC-associated subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) not amenable to curative surgical resection (EXIST-1 trial).

onc201_dmg.name: H3 K27-Altered Targeted & Clinical Trial Pathways
onc201_dmg.summary: Evaluate for DRD2/ClpP agonist (dordaviprone/ONC201) trials, GD2 CAR-T therapy, and specialized pediatric/adult neuro-oncology clinical protocols.

li_fraumeni_shh_tp53.name: Germline TP53 / Li-Fraumeni Counseling
li_fraumeni_shh_tp53.summary: Medulloblastoma, SHH-activated and TP53-mutant carries a high rate of germline TP53 mutation; refer urgently to cancer genetics and account for elevated radiation-induced secondary malignancy risk.

cdkn2ab_idh_glioma.name: CDKN2A/B Homozygous Deletion in IDH-Mutant Glioma
cdkn2ab_idh_glioma.summary: Defines CNS WHO grade 4 in Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant regardless of histology (cIMPACT-NOW Update 5); in Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, grading remains histological and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion is an adverse prognostic marker that may support CNS WHO grade 3 only in histologically borderline/equivocal cases.

tert_cdkn2ab_meningioma.name: TERT Promoter Mutation & CDKN2A/B Homozygous Deletion in Meningioma
tert_cdkn2ab_meningioma.summary: Each biomarker independently establishes CNS WHO grade 3 meningioma in WHO CNS5, predicting rapid recurrence and poor survival even with histologically grade 1 morphology.

h3k27me3_prognostic.name: H3 K27me3 Loss (Epigenetic Biomarker)
h3k27me3_prognostic.summary: Defines Posterior fossa group A (PFA) ependymoma and H3 K27-altered DMG; in meningioma, H3 K27me3 loss predicts significantly higher recurrence risk.

vignettes.label: Molecular GBM (IDH-wt, TERT+, Histologically Low-Grade)
vignettes.description: 64-year-old with non-enhancing diffusely infiltrating astrocytic glioma lacking necrosis and MVP, but IDH-wildtype with TERT promoter mutation and MGMT promoter methylation -> Molecular upgrade to Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.

vignettes.label: Histologically Low-Grade IDH-wt Astrocytoma with EGFR Amp -> Molecular GBM Grade 4
vignettes.description: 61-year-old with bland infiltrating astrocytoma (no necrosis, no MVP) harboring IDH-wildtype status, EGFR amplification, and +7/-10 copy-number change -> Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.

vignettes.label: IDH-Mutant Astrocytoma with Homozygous CDKN2A/B Deletion -> Grade 4
vignettes.description: 39-year-old with IDH1 R132H-mutant, ATRX-lost, 1p/19q-intact astrocytoma showing mitotic activity without necrosis or MVP, but homozygous CDKN2A/B deletion -> Molecular upgrade to Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4.

vignettes.label: IDH-Mutant 1p/19q-Codeleted Oligodendroglioma Grade 2 (Vorasidenib-Eligible)
vignettes.description: 44-year-old with frontal non-enhancing glioma: IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted, ATRX retained, CDKN2A/B intact, low mitotic activity -> Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, CNS WHO grade 2.

vignettes.label: Midline H3 K27-Altered DMG Grade 4 (Low-Grade Biopsy Override)
vignettes.description: 11-year-old with pontine/thalamic infiltrative lesion showing bland astrocytic histology on stereotactic biopsy, but H3 K27M mutation and global H3 K27me3 loss -> Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered, CNS WHO grade 4.

vignettes.label: Histologically Grade 1 Meningioma with TERT Promoter Mutation -> Grade 3
vignettes.description: 58-year-old with recurrent convexity meningioma showing 1 mitosis/10 HPF, no brain invasion, and no atypical features, but harboring a TERT promoter mutation -> Molecular upgrade to Meningioma, CNS WHO grade 3.

vignettes.label: Myxopapillary Ependymoma -> CNS WHO Grade 2 (CNS5 Upgrade)
vignettes.description: 32-year-old with filum terminale mass showing papillary fronds with perivascular myxoid cores -> Myxopapillary ependymoma, CNS WHO grade 2 (upgraded from grade 1 in 2016).

vignettes.label: Medulloblastoma, SHH-Activated and TP53-Mutant (Li-Fraumeni Counseling)
vignettes.description: 10-year-old with cerebellar hemispheric tumor showing large cell/anaplastic histology, SHH activation, TP53 mutation, and MYCN amplification -> High-risk SHH TP53-mutant medulloblastoma, CNS WHO grade 4.

vignettes.label: Glioblastoma, NOS (IDH Testing Not Performed)
vignettes.description: 68-year-old with ring-enhancing temporal mass showing necrosis and microvascular proliferation where IDH molecular testing could not be completed due to depleted tissue -> Glioblastoma, NOS, CNS WHO grade 4.

vignettes.label: Diffuse Astrocytic Glioma, IDH-Wildtype, NEC (Negative Molecular GBM Panel)
vignettes.description: 47-year-old with histologically low-grade IDH-wildtype, H3-wildtype diffuse astrocytic glioma in which TERT promoter, EGFR amplification, and +7/-10 are all negative -> NEC (avoid forcing GBM; perform methylation profiling).
